intro: Two concept families that compose without coupling. WORKFLOWS produce records (triage, analysis, launch packaging, thumbnails). BI SOURCES expose the data substrate the workflows read. Each workflow declares an ALS shape — what record it writes — so any consumer can read it later without re-deriving.

workflows.name: Project Triage
workflows.goal: Read every project, classify state, flag investigation needs.
signals: Stage status (recording / editing / done) from FliHub project metadata
Has intro segment? (chapter 01 with label matching intro|opening|hook)
Has outro segment? (final chapter with label matching outro|wrap|cta)
workflows.als_framing: Each project gets a triage-record.md with frontmatter for the signals (booleans + enums) and prose body for notes. Bulk run iterates the project list, writes one record per project. Missing-thing signals route to operator-gated sub-workflows (generate / investigate / manual) — operator decisions, not agent decisions.

workflows.name: Missing SRT
workflows.goal: When a recording has no transcript: branch to auto-generate, investigate, or accept manual.
signals: FliHub missing-transcripts=true flag on a recording
Recording file present but no .srt/.txt sibling
workflows.als_framing: Operator-gate branch off the triage record. Three advance transitions: generate (Whisper), investigate (why missing), manual (accept as-is). Branch outcome appended to triage record body section.

workflows.name: Missing Intro / Outro
workflows.goal: When a project lacks bookend segments: insert from template, re-record, or mark as fragment.
signals: No chapter 01 segment with intro/opening/hook label
No final chapter with outro/wrap/cta label
workflows.als_framing: Operator-gate branch off the triage record. Three advance transitions: template-insert, re-record-required, accept-as-fragment. Outcome recorded against the project's triage record.

workflows.name: Dormant Scan
workflows.goal: Flag any project with no edits in N days for review.
signals: No mtime on recordings/ or edit-1st/ within N days
No FliHub activity within N days
workflows.als_framing: Per-project boolean field on the triage record (dormant: true/false) plus last_activity timestamp. Bulk-run output, no per-record gate.

workflows.name: Core Idea
workflows.goal: Extract the essence, key value, and promise of every video — independently of any launch run.
workflows.als_framing: core_idea field on the per-project analysis-record.md. Persists at one path per project regardless of how it was produced. Distinct from launch state — analysis can be regenerated, batch-overwritten, or read by triage / launch / visualisation without touching launch state.

workflows.name: Hooks
workflows.goal: Generate 3–5 hook angles per project — the framing surface for both title and thumbnail.
signals: Kickoff segment transcript (the -1- segment of each chapter)
workflows.als_framing: hooks[] array field on analysis-record.md. Each hook is a candidate framing — title and thumbnail derive from the same hook independently (hook-centric fan-out, not title→thumbnail).

workflows.name: Audience Classification
workflows.goal: Per known audience term, classify whether it's primary, secondary, or hidden in the video.
workflows.als_framing: audience[] structured field on analysis-record.md, each entry with term + tier (primary/secondary/hidden). Drives subliminal text-layer choice in thumbnail workflow.

workflows.name: Identity Cues
workflows.goal: Surface tribal terms and identity markers (BMAD-style language) the video already speaks to.
signals: Transcript scan for known identity vocabulary
workflows.als_framing: identity[] field on analysis-record.md. Feeds related-video suggestions and can subtly inform thumbnail subliminal text.

workflows.name: Title Development
workflows.goal: Generate ten title candidates per video; operator selects a shortlist.
workflows.als_framing: titles-record.md with frontmatter list of 10 candidates and a body section for selection rationale. Operator-gate state: awaiting-title-shortlist. Sub-record of the per-video launch session.

workflows.name: Chapter Refinement
workflows.goal: Promote recording-time chapter labels to publish-quality YouTube chapter titles.
signals: Filename labels (the BI is in the convention — chapter labels already set at record time)
Per-segment SRT timing for chapter timestamps
workflows.als_framing: Inline states on the launch Delamain (not a separate Delamain — chapters are part of the main flow). AI suggests cleaner labels, operator approves at awaiting-chapter-review gate. Timing adjustment is a tool call, not a workflow state.

workflows.name: Description Packaging
workflows.goal: Assemble synopsis + chapters + slots (affiliate / legal / CTA / branding).
signals: Static config slot content (affiliate links, legal boilerplate, CTA)
workflows.als_framing: description-record.md with named body sections per slot. Operator-gate at awaiting-review for final approval. Maps cleanly to spec §9 declared slots.

workflows.name: Related Videos
workflows.goal: Lightweight related-video suggestions to slot into the description.
workflows.als_framing: related[] field on description-record.md. Lightweight by design — v1 is not a cross-video pattern tracker.

workflows.name: Keyword Tags
workflows.goal: Generate 10–15 tags for the YouTube tags field.
workflows.als_framing: tags[] field on the launch session record. Pure agent output, no operator gate.

workflows.name: Design Conversation
workflows.goal: Establish concept, contrast mode (Explain/Intrigue, Abstract/Concrete, Calm/Dramatic, Parallel) and text layer plan (none / primary / subliminal).
workflows.als_framing: Separate ALS module (FliThumb is a composable, not a sub-Delamain). thumbnail-concept-record.md with contrast-mode field, text-layer enum, and prose body for the design rationale. Operator-driven conversation.

workflows.name: Exploration Builds
workflows.goal: Generate 10–20 cheap candidate thumbnails to widen the design space before committing.
signals: Concept + contrast mode from the design conversation
workflows.als_framing: exploration[] array on the thumbnail record. Cheap renders, not production assets. Output is the candidate pool for the next gate.

workflows.name: Selection
workflows.goal: Lock 5–8 pairs from the exploration set as the shortlist.
workflows.als_framing: selected[] field on the thumbnail record. Operator-gate at awaiting-thumbnail-shortlist. Pairs (not single thumbnails) so A/B testing is built in.

workflows.name: Final Builds
workflows.goal: Render 3 production finals + 1–2 backups from the locked shortlist.
workflows.als_framing: finals[] field with paths to rendered assets. Marks the thumbnail record complete and signals the launch Delamain it can transition to awaiting-review.

bi_sources.name: FliHub
bi_sources.description: FliHub is BI, not just an API. It already encodes intelligence in its data shape — chapter/segment naming, recording metadata, missing-transcript detection — so workflows should consume that intelligence rather than re-derive it. Runs on port 5101 from ~/dev/ad/flivideo/flihub/.
bi_sources.answers: Questions like: which projects exist? what's missing transcripts? what chapters does this video have and at what timestamps? what's the LLM-ready bundle for this project? Where do I write outputs back?
provides: GET /projects — the project list, driver for any bulk workflow
GET /projects/:code/transcripts?include=content — full transcript content per recording
GET /projects/:code/chapters?format=text — YouTube-ready chapter list with timestamps
GET /projects/:code/recordings?missing-transcripts=true — direct missing-thing signal
GET /projects/:code/recordings?chapter=N — per-chapter recording group
GET /projects/:code/export?format=text — LLM-ready bundle for ingestion
POST /projects/:code/inbox/write — where ALS writes outputs back

bi_sources.name: Recording Filesystem
bi_sources.description: The on-disk layout under ~/dev/video-projects/v-appydave/<code>/ where the naming convention <chapter>-<segment>-<label> IS the BI. Chapter boundaries, chapter labels, kickoff segments, and per-chapter effort signal are all encoded for free at recording time — before any AI runs.
bi_sources.answers: Questions like: where do chapters break? what's the kickoff segment of a chapter? how dense is each chapter (segment count as effort proxy)? how do I concatenate transcripts at chapter level?
provides: recording-transcripts/<chapter>-<segment>-<label>.{srt,txt,json}
recordings/<chapter>-<segment>-<label>.mov
Chapter boundaries — derived from chapter-number changes in filenames
Chapter labels — set by hand at record time, candidate YouTube chapter titles
Kickoff segments — the -1- segment of each chapter sets narrative tone
Effort signal — segment count per chapter (1 = brief, 21 = deep)
.awb.json — legacy workflow state on ~6 projects (read-only artifact)

bi_sources.name: Brand Docs (DESIGN.md)
bi_sources.description: The AppyDave brand source — palette, voice, design language, typography. Owned by the operator and version-controlled with the brand. Read by any workflow that produces visible output (thumbnails, descriptions, on-screen text).
bi_sources.answers: Questions like: what's the AppyDave palette? what's the brand voice? which typefaces are sanctioned? what design language applies to this surface?
provides: AppyDave brand palette (cream / linen / brown / amber / yellow accents)
Brand voice and tone guidelines
Sanctioned typography (Oswald / Roboto / Roboto Mono)
Design language patterns for visible surfaces

bi_sources.name: Third-Party Brand Repo
bi_sources.description: External brand assets the workflows reference but don't own — Anthropic / Claude / Gemini logos and colour systems. Used wherever the video discusses third-party products and the thumbnail or description needs accurate brand representation.
bi_sources.answers: Questions like: what's the official Claude logo? what colour is Anthropic's brand? how do I represent Gemini in a thumbnail without violating brand guidelines?
provides: Anthropic / Claude logos and brand colours
Gemini logos and brand palette
Third-party brand usage rules (where documented)

bi_sources.name: Static Config
bi_sources.description: Hand-curated configuration that doesn't belong in any other system — the canonical audiences[] list and the related-videos pool. Lightweight by design; v1 explicitly avoids analytics dashboards or cross-video pattern tracking.
bi_sources.answers: Questions like: what audiences am I classifying against? what's the pool of related videos to suggest from? what slot content (affiliate / legal / CTA) gets stamped into descriptions?
provides: audiences[] — known audience terms for classification
related-videos[] — pool for description suggestions
Description slot content (affiliate links, legal, CTA boilerplate)
